texts.description: This layer depicts the service area boundaries of electric utilities in Oregon. We have used data from the utilities and online maps to compile this data layer. We are aware that service territories can overlap and we have noted that in certain areas when we find GIS data that confirms the overlap. Despite our best efforts to keep this data up to date, this layer should not be used to make critical decisions unless the data has been ground verified. At this time we update this layer 2-3 times per year as we get new information. If you are aware of an issue with this data, please contact Jim Gores at jim.gores@energy.oregon.gov.
texts.copyrightText: Layer created and maintained by Jim Gores at the Oregon Department of Energy, jim.gores@energy.oregon.gov.

texts.description: This data is a graphic representation of electric utility service territories. The file has not been certified by a Professional Surveyor. This data is not suitable for legal purposes. The purpose of this data is to provide a generalized statewide view of electric service territories. The data does not include individual or commercial releases. A release is an agreement between adjoining utilities that release customers from one utility to be served by the adjoining utility. A customer release does not change the territory boundary. The file has been compiled from numerous sources and as such contains errors. The data only contains the electric utility service territories and the name of the utility.

texts.description: The UNOFFICIAL Investor-Owned Utility (IOU) certified electric service area boundaries geospatial data layer has been created to display the geographic extent that utilities deliver electricity. The official certified electric service area boundaries are on file as county mylar maps and are available upon request at Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) Central Records. Any amendments to those boundaries since the mylar maps were retired in the 1970's are recorded in PUCT Dockets.Unless otherwise noted, data was submitted by the electric utilities; Data edited by Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) Infrastructure Staff Gary Horton (GIS Specialist) and Reginald Tuvilla (Electric Infrastructure Analyst) on July 22, 2020; Data delivered to the PUCT by Miguel Pavon, who had been working with ongoing edits to service area boundaries at TxGIO (formerly TNRIS); Original data source Platts.
